name: Warionex
summary: A medieval high-fantasy adventure sandbox built around Bloom Level-Up: dragons, monsters, bosses, magic, knights, new biomes, decor, shaders and Fresh Animations, with Better Combat. Minecraft 1.20.1 (Forge).
_comment: FreshOrangeSlices' Warionex (named LegionWareX until 2026-10-30; its own ids, folders and commands keep legionwarex) (2026-10-26), from the Medieval High Fantasy master list and goals docs: a sandbox full of optional content, no required ending, dangerous but not miserable, multiplayer first. Combat route: Better Combat (not Epic Fight); Better Mob Combat is shelved (its mob animation hook crashes the server on creatures from Mowzie's, Migamigos, Cataclysm, Legendary Monsters and Monster Expansion, and with the whole pack on vanilla wolves too; its last build is from January 2025). After the first playtest: Novum's Altitude out (its sky effects made the world disorienting), Ice and Fire out (its dragons wreck buildings, and its 1.20.1 build is a beta), Mowzie's Mobs out, and a bosses layer in their place. Magic: Iron's Spells, plus the RPG Series' Paladins & Priests and Rogues & Warriors (no Wizards, Elemental Wizards or Archers). Voice chat: Simple Voice Chat, set up ahead of time so friends join with nothing extra to do (FreshOrangeSlices, 2026-10-30, reversing the first call of no voice chat): no setup wizard, push-to-talk on Caps Lock, plus Sound Physics Remastered (voices echo and muffle) and Voiceless Survival (hostile mobs hear you talk). Mods are in cumulative layers so CI can tell which layer breaks what; the shipped pack is every layer. Forge 47.4.28 (1.20.1's recommended; Iron's Spells and others need 47.4+). Modrinth projects by slug (newest 1.20.1 Forge release or beta; required dependencies are added automatically, and the few a mod needs without saying so on Modrinth, such as Iron's Lib, are listed next to it; Migamigos' Framework is CurseForge-only, so it's packed inside). Bloom and the CurseForge-only mods ('external') are packed inside, which is fine for sharing with friends but not for publishing.

layers.name: core
layers._comment: Bloom with Better Combat, Combat Roll (the pack's one dodge roll, on Z: its roll animates through Player Animator, which Better Combat brings too) and the Fresh Animations set (the earlier Forge pack; FA+ Spiders out, FreshOrangeSlices found it broken in play, so spiders are vanilla), plus the performance mods, since they change how everything renders: Embeddium, ModernFix, FerriteCore, Clumps, Entity Culling (doesn't draw what's out of sight), ImmediatelyFast (faster HUD and text drawing), AI Improvements (cheaper mob AI), Let Me Despawn (mobs that picked up items still despawn, dropping them), and for the server, Chunky (pre-generate the world) and spark (find what lags). Open Loader puts the pack's own data pack (pack_data) into every world and the server.

external.name: FTB Library
external._why: Playtest patch, chunk 6: the quest book (FTB Quests) runs on FTB Library and FTB Teams (FTB's own mods are on CurseForge only; Architectury is on Modrinth). Each player starts in a team of their own, so their quest progress is their own unless they make a party.

external.name: FTB Quests
external._why: The quest book (the book button at the top-left of the inventory). Its chapters are written in pack/quests/ and built into config/ftbquests/quests by pack/quest_book.py, with only what each layer's mods have.

layers.name: creatures
layers._comment: Creatures, bosses and companions, and the spawn and structure control that keeps them memorable instead of everywhere. Zoni's Companions (FreshOrangeSlices' pick, beside Migamigos) are only summoned, from devices players craft, never found in the wild; its Ultimate Summon Device (catches any mob, bosses included) is taken out and its creative-only items are hidden (pack_data). Harder mobs mainly by day (playtest patch, chunk 5), each with its own spawns off or low so they come as the add-on's daytime sentinels and in their own structures: Undead Unleashed – Continued (Dreadknights, Wraiths, Flamebreathers), Born in Chaos (about 80 mobs, its graves, caravans and towers; its Halloween and winter mobs stay on) and Dungeon Denizens (classic fantasy: orcs, skeleton warriors, gargoyles, wights; CurseForge only, with its library gottsch's Monster Manual, and GottschCore).

external.name: Fauna Engine
external._why: Book of Dragons 1.4's library (mod id liberanimalium; CurseForge only, not listed as a dependency on Modrinth)

external.name: Dungeon Denizens
external._why: Playtest patch, chunk 5: harder mobs by day (CurseForge only). 2.0 runs on gottsch's Monster Manual and GottschCore (on Modrinth)

external.name: gottsch's Monster Manual
external._why: Dungeon Denizens 2.0's library of mob classes (CurseForge only)

layers.name: magic-and-gear
layers._comment: Iron's Spells as the mage, the RPG Series' Paladins & Priests and Rogues & Warriors (Spell Engine comes with them), weapons and armor, and the recipe glue for all of it. Marium's Soulslike Weaponry is on test (power creep).

layers.name: animation-and-qol
layers._comment: The rest of the visual stack (Punchy! stays unless testing shows it fights Better Combat; Oculus, the Forge port of Iris, with Complementary Unbound picked, Solas to swap to, and MakeUp Ultra Fast for weaker PCs), and the quality-of-life and multiplayer mods. Keybind Atlas replaced KeyVision (FreshOrangeSlices' playtest: KeyVision took over the Controls screen and had no mouse buttons); it's a separate keyboard-and-mouse map on Ctrl+K, so the normal Controls list is back.

layers.name: bosses
layers._comment: Bosses in place of Ice and Fire and Mowzie's Mobs (first playtest): L_Ender's Cataclysm (dungeon bosses), Legendary Monsters (roaming early, middle and late game bosses), Bosses'Rise (Souls-like bosses), The Graveyard (graveyards, crypts and their undead) and Illager Invasion (new illagers to fight), Bosses Oddities (more unusual bosses; CurseForge-only, packed inside) and GTBC's Cataclysmic Boss UI (a screen before each Cataclysm boss fight with its lore, attacks and tips), the last two FreshOrangeSlices' picks. CI summons every one of their creatures with the rest of the pack.

layers.name: world-and-decor
layers._comment: Copper Age Backport (FreshOrangeSlices, 2026-10-29: copper tools and armor, which 1.20.1 doesn't have, and the rest of its copper lineup: chests, shelves, bars, chains, lanterns, torches, bulbs, doors and the copper golem; held at its last release). Biomes O' Plenty for the world (FreshOrangeSlices' pick; Terralith's biomes felt too big), and Decorative Blocks and Handcrafted for building (beams, braziers, chains, lattices and seats; vanilla-style furniture). BOP's Nether is cut back (config_files): Visceral Heap and Withered Abyss are off, and its Nether regions weigh 5 against vanilla's 10 (BOP's default is 13, more than half the Nether). Every Compat (Wood Good) makes the decor in BOP's woods too (and in any other mod's woods it knows); its blocks have their own creative tab.

config_files._comment: For both sides (the server, and the worlds a player makes; Forge copies defaultconfigs into each new world). A safety net: an entity or block entity that errors while ticking is removed and logged instead of crashing the server. Legionary's Unbreakable boss shoots flaming skulls and magma blocks whose code needs a client-only class, so each one crashes a dedicated server on its first tick (found by the mob check); with this they fizzle instead.
config_files._biomesoplenty: BOP's own files with two Nether biomes off (Visceral Heap's flesh, Withered Abyss's void pits) and its Nether region weight 5 instead of 13 (vanilla's is 10), so about two thirds of the Nether stays vanilla. The Overworld is BOP's default.
config_files.config/biomesoplenty/generation.toml:
[nether]
	#The weighting of bop biome regions in the nether.
	bop_nether_region_weight = 5
	#The weighting of rare bop biome regions in the nether.
	bop_nether_rare_region_weight = 2

[overworld]
	#The weighting of primary bop biome regions in the overworld.
	bop_primary_overworld_region_weight = 10
	#The weighting of rare bop biome regions in the overworld.
	bop_overworld_rare_region_weight = 2
	#The weighting of secondary bop biome regions in the overworld.
	bop_secondary_overworld_region_weight = 8
config_files._mutantmonsters: Mutant Monsters' spawn weights, as a share of each vanilla counterpart's: 10% (default 5%; FreshOrangeSlices: twice as common). Forge fills in the rest of the file.
config_files._bloomlevelup: Bloom's XP, half as fast again in every category (FreshOrangeSlices' playtest: XP gain faster overall). Titan Hide's innate armor +4 instead of Bloom's +2 (FreshOrangeSlices, 2026-10-29: getting armor in the pack is risky and some mobs come out swinging axes, so the no-armor Major is an early answer: 8 armor, four plates, at 0 Defense, past a leather set's 7 and well under iron's 15). Shovel Mastery's treasure 3% per dug block instead of 10% (about 5% at 100 Yield; FreshOrangeSlices: too generous). Only these lines are set; Bloom fills in the rest of its file with its own defaults when it loads, and writes them back.
config_files._dodge: One dodge in the pack (FreshOrangeSlices): Combat Roll. Its server settings: you can't be hit for the whole roll (8 ticks; its default is 0), a 3 s cooldown (4 s by default; tuned in play) and a roll even while the weapon recharges (Better Combat's swings would otherwise block most rolls in a fight). Bosses'Rise's roll (a server setting, read from defaultconfigs/ by every new world) and Monster Expansion's (a common setting) are switched off.
config_files.defaultconfigs/block_factorys_bosses-ser:
["Gameplay Changes"]
	"Can players use the Roll ability" = false
config_files._easymsc: Easy Mob Spawn Control's files (its in-game menu edits the same ones). Shybroom no longer lives in villages (FreshOrangeSlices found her in none of 10): its structure spawn lists are left empty, and she spawns in plains instead (spawns.add.migamigos_shybroom). The roaming Queen of Orchid and Draugr Boss despawn once idle for 2 minutes with no player within 64 blocks (unless name-tagged or in sight), and at most one of each is loaded at a time; Dungeon Denizens' Wood Golem despawns the same way, and one roaming Sir Pumpkinhead is loaded at a time.
config_files._easymsc_rules: Spawn rules for mobs whose mod gives them none (no SpawnPlacements entry: a natural spawn then ignores light, time and ground, so the Queen of Orchid turned up in daylight; FreshOrangeSlices). Also for mobs whose rules allow daylight: Illager Invasion's illagers use vanilla's patrol rules (any light), so out of their structures they spawned by day (FreshOrangeSlices). Both rules hold in the Overworld only (elsewhere the mobs keep their own rules: the Graveyard's corrupted illagers in the Nether). Monsters (the roaming bosses, Cataclysm's draugrs, Iron's catacombs zombies, Illager Invasion's marauders, provokers, bashers and alchemists, Myths & Legends' possessed armor): night (13000-23000), sky light 8 or more (outdoors or under trees, not caves), no torchlight, standing on ground (the block below). The Graveyard's acolytes and corrupted pillagers and vindicators (in swampy, magical and dark biomes, spawns.add.dark_crew): whenever it's dark (light 7 or less, as at night or under thick cover; FreshOrangeSlices), no torchlight, some sky (not caves), on the ground. The add-on's daytime war bands come as patrols and aren't held to these rules (FreshOrangeSlices: illagers by day are fine as war bands). Skarrier's Breacher and Dragger (cave mobs whose rules let them out by day): no sky light and no torchlight, so caves only, at any hour. Born in Chaos's pumpkin folk, the Harvest Court (all year now, FreshOrangeSlices): night_ground, so they keep to the fields at night, not caves. Dungeon Denizens' Headless (its rules allow daylight): night_ground. Never on animals: Easy Mob Spawn Control checks a rule against the world itself, and animals spawn while chunks generate, so the check waits on a chunk that can't load until it's done (the server hung starting, build #282). The pack test fails when a mob the pack adds has neither rules of its own nor one of these.

pins._comment: Mods held at a version, even with --update (the lock only holds the last tested): each with why, so it can go once a fixed version is out.

backport-copper-age.why: its last release (2025-12-01); 0.1.5 and 0.1.5.1-pre (2026-10) are betas

azurelib.why: Book of Dragons 1.4 and its Fauna Engine ask for exactly 3.2.0 (only they use AzureLib)

keybind-atlas.why: 2.1.0 (2026-10-28) isn't remapped for a real game (built with development names), so the client crashes while loading

pack_data._comment: Warionex's own data pack, loaded into every world (new and old) and the server by Open Loader, from config/openloader/data/legionwarex: the recipes the pack takes out (each replaced by one that never loads), the items it takes out of the game (removed_items: their recipes, loot table entries and JEI listing, found in the mods' own files when the pack is built), and the items it hides from JEI (the c:hidden_from_recipe_viewers tag). Grouped by reason. CI checks the recipes are gone and the hidden items carry the tag (pack-data, from Bloom's registry dump).
pack_data.name: legionwarex
pack_data.description: Warionex: recipes the pack takes out, items it hides from JEI

removed_items._comment: FreshOrangeSlices' armory trim (2026-10-28, from the LegionWareX Armory page: every weapon sorted into own skill, own effect, stat bonus or nothing of its own). 230 weapons out: their recipes never load, the loot tables that name them are rewritten without them, and they're hidden from JEI. Ones a mod drops from its own code (some boss drops) can only be hidden; the pack summary lists them. Kept on purpose: the six Epic Knights shortswords the bigger swords are made from, the Knight's Sword (makes the Knight Summoner), the Decrepit Flamberge (repaired into the Legionnaire Flamberge), Monster Expansion's wooden mace and spear (Hunter's Notes) and Rimescourge (a quest reward).

recipe_edits._comment: Mods' recipes changed in place (the recipe from its jar, items swapped).

zonis_companions:summon_item_craft.why: Zoni's empty summon device: 8 amethyst shards around an iron block instead of a diamond block (FreshOrangeSlices: a bit easier)

worldgen._comment: Worldgen files the pack replaces, at data/<namespace>/worldgen/<path>.json. They only shape chunks made after the change: an old world gets seams where new chunks meet old ones, so these are for new worlds. The pack test reads the terrain the server would make (the add-on's terrain survey, -Dlegionwarex.terrain) beside vanilla's for the same seed.

legionwarex:density_function/erosion_noi.why: Vanilla's erosion noise, as vanilla's minecraft:overworld/erosion reads it (unchanged), named so the pack's erosion below can use it twice.

minecraft:density_function/overworld/ero.why: Fewer and lower mountains (FreshOrangeSlices: too many of them, and too big; oceans are fine). Erosion is the noise that decides how rugged land is: low erosion is where peaks and slopes rise, both in the terrain's height and in which biome goes there, so pulling its low end in gives fewer mountains everywhere, Biomes O' Plenty's land included. Below 0 vanilla's value x 0.65 (-1 becomes -0.65), 0 and above unchanged: the lowest band (below -0.78, where the highest peaks rise) is gone, the next (below -0.375, peaks and mountains) about halves, and flat land, windswept hills and swamps (the top) don't change. A first try (x 0.9 + 0.1 everywhere, build #295) lowered the peaks but pushed land into the windswept hills' band, so the share of mountain biomes hardly fell. Continentalness (land and sea) is untouched.

data_edits._comment: A mod's own data file with some of its values changed (the rest, and a mod update's new ones, stay): data/<namespace>/<path>.json.

bookofdragons:spawn_settings.why: Book of Dragons 1.4's dragons out in the wild, away from roosts (new in 1.4), at half its numbers so dragons stay a find: at most 7 in the world (its default 14) plus 2 per extra player (3), and 2 within 128 blocks (4). The roosts, doubled earlier, stay the main place to meet one.

spawns._comment: FreshOrangeSlices' playtest (2 hours, almost no modded mobs): the pack's natural spawns, aimed at about 1 in 5 of the mobs that spawn at night in every overworld biome (Biomes O' Plenty's included) being modded, about 1 in 20 being a structure's regulars out in biomes that fit them, bosses only in their lairs, at the same mob cap (vanilla's). Counted by mobs, not weight: vanilla monsters come in fours, most modded ones alone. Skarrier Mobs listed 15 of its mobs in every biome of every dimension at high weights, though each only spawns in one biome, underground, or after the Wither is beaten, so about half of all spawn picks failed; those are put back only where they can spawn. Graveyard and Cataclysm pick their biomes by tags, which only named vanilla biomes; the tags now take BOP's in. Mutant Monsters' weights are in its config (config_files). The pack test reports each biome's modded share (pack-spawns).

quiet.why: Biomes the pack adds no monsters to: vanilla's own peaceful ones (the Deep Dark is the Warden's, Mushroom Fields have none) and Biomes O' Plenty's (Auroral Garden has none, Mystic Grove few).

monsterexpansion:skrythe_biomes.why: Skrythe (750 health) spawns from its lair when the lair generates (one per 60x60 chunks where the biome fits); the lair could go in almost any overworld biome. Mountains only (FreshOrangeSlices).

graveyard:ghoul_spawns.why: Emptied: ghouls come from the pack's own spawns below (all land but quiet biomes).

graveyard:revenant_spawns.why: Emptied: revenants come from the pack's own spawns below (every snowy biome, smaller packs).

graveyard:nightmare_spawns.why: Emptied: nightmares come from the pack's own spawns below (open, dry and high land).

cataclysm:koboleton_spawn.why: Emptied: koboletons come from the pack's own spawns below (every dry biome).

bookofdragons:has_roost_cliff.why: Book of Dragons' cliff roosts (Night Fury, Skrill): vanilla's snowy peaks only; now every peak and mountain, BOP's Crag and Jade Cliffs too (FreshOrangeSlices: dragons were rare and far out).

bookofdragons:has_roost_cave.why: Cave roosts (Gronckle, Whispering Death): vanilla's windswept hills, Stony Peaks and Meadow; now every hill and mountain (BOP's Highland, Crag, Jade Cliffs, Moor, Volcano).

bookofdragons:has_roost_glade.why: Glade roosts (Deadly Nadder, Hideous Zippleback): vanilla's old-growth forests and two jungles; now every forest, taiga and jungle.

bookofdragons:has_roost_wetland.why: Wetland roosts (Hideous Zippleback): vanilla's swamps and Mushroom Fields; now every swamp (BOP's Bayou, Bog, Floodplain, Marsh, Moor, Muskeg, Wetland).

bookofdragons:has_roost_barrens.why: Barrens roosts (Monstrous Nightmare, Gronckle): vanilla's desert, badlands and savannas; now every dry biome and savanna.

block_factorys_bosses:dragon_tower.why: Structures (FreshOrangeSlices: too far apart in BOP land): Bosses'Rise's dragon tower: vanilla jungles, swamps, plains, savanna and windswept hills; BOP's too.

block_factorys_bosses:sandworm_nest.why: Bosses'Rise's sandworm nest: vanilla Desert only; every desert.

block_factorys_bosses:yeti_hideout.why: Bosses'Rise's yeti hideout: vanilla Snowy Plains only; every snowy biome.

graveyard:has_structure/altar.why: The Graveyard's altar: Ice Spikes and Snowy Plains; every snowy biome.

graveyard:has_structure/large_graveyard.why: The Graveyard's large graveyard: vanilla taigas; every taiga.

graveyard:has_structure/medium_graveyard.why: Medium graveyard: vanilla forests; every forest.

graveyard:has_structure/memorial_tree.why: Memorial tree: vanilla birch forests; BOP's birch-like ones.

graveyard:has_structure/overrun_desert_v.why: Overrun desert village: vanilla Desert; every desert.

graveyard:has_structure/overrun_plains_v.why: Overrun plains village: Plains and Meadow; every plain.

graveyard:has_structure/overrun_savanna_.why: Overrun savanna village: vanilla Savanna; every savanna.

graveyard:has_structure/overrun_snowy_vi.why: Overrun snowy village: vanilla Snowy Plains; BOP's snowy clearings and tundra.

graveyard:has_structure/overrun_taiga_vi.why: Overrun taiga village: vanilla Taiga; every taiga.

graveyard:has_structure/ruins.why: The Graveyard's ruins: vanilla Forest; every forest.

graveyard:has_structure/small_desert_gra.why: Small desert grave: vanilla Desert; every desert.
Small desert graveyard: vanilla Desert; every desert.

graveyard:has_structure/small_mountain_g.why: Small mountain grave: vanilla peaks and slopes; every mountain.

graveyard:has_structure/small_savanna_gr.why: Small savanna grave: vanilla savannas and badlands; every savanna and badlands, BOP's dry lands.

illagerinvasion:has_structure/firecaller.why: Illager Invasion's firecaller hut: vanilla badlands; BOP's wastelands and volcanic land too.

illagerinvasion:has_structure/illusioner.why: Illusioner tower: Dark Forest, taigas and Swamp; every taiga and swamp, and Ominous Woods.

illagerinvasion:has_structure/sorcerer_h.why: Sorcerer hut: Dark Forest; BOP's Ominous Woods and dead forests.

legendary_monsters:has_structure/mossy_t.why: Legendary Monsters' mossy temple (Overgrown Colossus): two vanilla jungles; every jungle and rainforest.

legendary_monsters:has_structure/ruined_.why: Legendary Monsters' ruined pyramid: vanilla Desert; every desert.

monsterexpansion:rakoth_biomes.why: Monster Expansion's Rakoth (its spawn marker): vanilla desert and badlands; every desert and dry land.

mythsandlegends:old_camp_biomes.why: Myths & Legends' old camp (possessed armor): Flower Forest and Meadow; BOP's flower fields and meadows too.

structure_sets._comment: Book of Dragons' roosts (one dragon each; the roost brings a new one a day after it's killed or tamed) about 30% closer together, so twice as many per area (FreshOrangeSlices: double). Spacing and separation in chunks; the mod's were cliff 32/16, cave 20/10, the others 24/12.
structure_sets._nether: The Nether's structures a quarter closer together, so nearly twice as many per area (FreshOrangeSlices: travelling there is dangerous, so they should be easier to find). Bosses'Rise's Underworld Arena (the Underworld Knight; huge) stays as it was, and so do fortresses and bastions (vanilla's nether_complexes): the arena keeps 8 chunks from them, so more of them would make it rarer. Legionary's Bastion Arena (the Unbreakable) was 320/128, one per 5000 Nether blocks: now 80/32.
structure_sets._ice_spider: Iron's Spells' Ice Spider Dens about twice as common (FreshOrangeSlices, 2026-10-29: hard to find): spacing 60 and separation 35 chunks, from 85 and 50, so one chance per about 960-block square instead of 1,360 (still only where that spot is snowy).

structure_spawns._comment: Mobs added to a structure's own spawns, as {entity: [weight, min, max]}. Forge 1.20.1 has no structure forge:add_spawns, so the structure is overridden: its JSON from the jars, else base (vanilla's own, which no jar carries), with the spawners added.

fortress_wither_skeletons.why: Fortresses: twice the wither skeletons (vanilla's weight 8 in fives, plus 8 more in fours to sixes), about half the fortress's mobs instead of a third, now that Cataclysm's Ignited Berserkers share it (still added on top) (FreshOrangeSlices).

harvest_court.why: Born in Chaos's pumpkin folk, the Harvest Court, all year (FreshOrangeSlices, 2026-10-30): its spawn rule only lets them out from 25 October to 7 November, so the add-on lets them out the rest of the year on the same terms, and Easy Mob Spawn Control keeps them to open ground at night. A very low chance beside the other families (FreshOrangeSlices, 2026-10-31): Mr. Pumpkin 15 to 3, Mrs Pumpkin 13 to 2, Senor Pumpkin 10 to 2, the Pumpkin Bruiser 10 to 2 (Born in Chaos's festival weights first). Sir Pumpkinhead roams on his own (roaming_sir_pumpkinhead).

roaming_sir_pumpkinhead.why: Roaming bosses: Born in Chaos's Sir Pumpkinhead, a mid-tier boss on his felsteed (FreshOrangeSlices, 2026-10-31), across the Overworld's open land at night; one loaded at a time (config_files). Below 30 health his horse is gone and he fights on foot (born_in_chaos_v1:sir_pumpkinhead_without_horse, 120 health).

chaos_land.why: Born in Chaos and Dungeon Denizens in the night's spawns (FreshOrangeSlices, 2026-10-31: the new mobs in the roster for normal spawns, but not the flies, maggots, termites, firelights, baby skeletons, orcs, ghouls, alligator gar, boulders or floating eyes, which the add-on keeps out of every world): the ones at home anywhere on land, at weights that make the new mobs about a tenth of the night's monsters together with the groups for their biomes.

chaos_open.why: Born in Chaos and Dungeon Denizens on open land: plains, savannas, meadows.

chaos_woods.why: Born in Chaos and Dungeon Denizens in forests and taigas: lumberjacks, hound packs, the Spiders Mother, grave zombies.

wood_golems.why: Dungeon Denizens' Wood Golem in vanilla's own forests (FreshOrangeSlices, 2026-10-31: a normal vanilla forest). It never despawns by itself: Easy Mob Spawn Control despawns it once idle with no player within 64 blocks (config_files).

chaos_dark.why: Born in Chaos and Dungeon Denizens in dark forests, swamps and dead woods: spirits, shadows, casters and the rarer knights.

chaos_swamp.why: Dungeon Denizens in swamps: acid skeletons and bloaters.

chaos_snow.why: Dungeon Denizens in snow: frost skeletons and wights.

chaos_dry.why: Born in Chaos and Dungeon Denizens in deserts and badlands: siamese skeletons, burning and magma skeletons.

chaos_high.why: Dungeon Denizens on mountains and hills: iron skeletons and gargoyles.

chaos_shore.why: Born in Chaos's Zombie Fisherman on beaches and stony shores.

chaos_caves.why: Dungeon Denizens' oozes, jellies and cave plants in dripstone and lush caves (the Deep Dark stays the Warden's).

chaos_waters.why: Born in Chaos's Corpse Fish in rivers and swamps, and the rare Glutton Fish (90 health) in rivers.

thornshell_crabs.why: Born in Chaos's Thornshell Crab on beaches and stony shores, as animals are.

ghouls.why: The Graveyard's ghouls (packs of 2-5): vanilla forests, taigas and swamps at weight 25; now all Overworld land (BOP's too) at 40. Overworld only: Forge's plain is_dry tag has the Nether and the End in it, so the pack uses is_dry/overworld (FreshOrangeSlices: no ghouls in the Nether).

revenants.why: The Graveyard's revenants: three vanilla snowy biomes in packs of 5-8 (weight 25); now every snowy biome, 3-5 at weight 12.

nightmares.why: The Graveyard's nightmares (alone): open land as before, and BOP's dry and high land; weight 20 (was 10).

koboletons.why: Cataclysm's koboletons (its desert ruins' regulars, 2-3): vanilla deserts, savannas and badlands at 15; now every dry biome, and savannas, at 35.

skarrier_caves.why: Underground in the dark (not the Deep Dark); Bowlder and Gorger only after the Wither is beaten. One Bowlder and one Wrought within 100 blocks.

skarrier_frozen_peaks.why: Freeze: vanilla Ice Spikes, Frozen Peaks and Snowy Slopes, after the Wither.

skarrier_ice_spikes.why: Frost: vanilla Ice Spikes, under the open sky.

skarrier_swamps.why: Slithers: vanilla Swamp and Mangrove Swamp, above Y 60 (at 120 they took over swamps).

skarrier_swamp.why: Gadlisk: vanilla Swamp, after the Wither.

skarrier_badlands.why: Viruleon (one within 100 blocks, after the Wither): vanilla badlands and desert.

skarrier_end.why: Voidrake: End Barrens and End Highlands, after the Wither.

monster_expansion_animals.why: Arborix and Kobeko (neutral, spawn like animals, in daylight too) as before, and in BOP's land biomes.

roaming_queen_of_orchid.why: Roaming bosses (FreshOrangeSlices: some bosses outside their structures, about 1 in 150, none with an intro or that break blocks): Bosses Oddities' Queen of Orchid, the mantis, in flowery biomes. She never despawns by herself: Easy Mob Spawn Control despawns her once idle and no player is within 64 blocks, and keeps one loaded at a time (config_files).

roaming_draugr_boss.why: Roaming bosses: Marium's Draugr Boss out of the Champion's Graves, in snowy biomes; one loaded at a time (config_files).

migamigos_claymore.why: Migamigos' Claymore (FreshOrangeSlices: companions more often): vanilla forests and Taiga at weight 1; now every forest and taiga, BOP's too, at 5 (the other animals add up to about 48; FreshOrangeSlices: more, since the strong mobs kill wild ones).

migamigos_wavelyn.why: Migamigos' Wavelyn: vanilla plains, birch forests and Cherry Grove; now every plain too, at 5.

migamigos_cocogoat.why: Migamigos' Cocogoat: Meadow, Stony Peaks, windswept hills and Cherry Grove; now every hill and mountain, at 5.

migamigos_pollypounce.why: Migamigos' Pollypounce: vanilla beaches, Stony Shore, Old Growth Birch Forest and Cherry Grove; now every beach too, at 5.

migamigos_shybroom.why: Migamigos' Shybroom: no wild spawn of her own (only her Spawn Broom); villages through Easy Mob Spawn Control never showed her, so the greener plains instead (FreshOrangeSlices), vanilla's and BOP's, at 5 like the others. Not the Meadow: few animals there, so the companions already outnumber them.

jungle_wild.why: Zombiflore (Skarrier, no spawn condition of its own): every jungle, not just vanilla's.

desert_bombers.why: Bombers (Legendary Monsters, vanilla Desert at 75): BOP's deserts too, fewer.

forest_crew.why: About 1 in 20: Illager Invasion's fort crew and Iron's Spells' catacombs zombies out of their forts and catacombs, in forests and taigas (The Graveyard's corrupted illagers moved to dark_crew).

village_crew.why: About 1 in 20: The Graveyard's tormented villagers out of its overrun villages, Illager Invasion's marauders and Iron's Spells' catacombs zombies on open land (the overrun villages' corrupted illagers moved to dark_crew).

snow_crew.why: About 1 in 20: Cataclysm's draugr out of the Frosted Prison, in snowy biomes.

mountain_crew.why: About 1 in 20: Myths & Legends' possessed armor out of its old camps, in mountains.

dark_crew.why: The Graveyard's corrupted illagers (FreshOrangeSlices: not with the war bands, in swampy, magical and dark biomes; whenever it's dark there, by Easy Mob Spawn Control's legionwarex_dark rule), about 1 in 10 there: every swamp, Dark Forest, BOP's Ominous Woods, Mystic Grove (quiet otherwise, haunted by these), Fungal Jungle and dead forests. Auroral Garden stays peaceful. Out of forests, open land and deserts, where they were 1 in 20.

swamp_crew.why: About 1 in 20: Illager Invasion's alchemists (they throw potions) in swamps.

unruled.why: Mobs the pack adds that have no spawn rules from their mod and can't get one from Easy Mob Spawn Control (animals: its rules hang world generation). Monster Expansion's Arborix spawned the same way from its own mod, at weight 1.

persistent.why: Monsters that never despawn but stay in the pack's spawns: Skarrier has them spawn in these vanilla biomes (Glowin in Dark Forests, Slithers in swamps), as they did before at higher weights; the Queen of Orchid, the Draugr Boss and Dungeon Denizens' Wood Golem get a despawn rule from Easy Mob Spawn Control. The pack test fails on any other added monster that never despawns.

conditional._comment: Mobs the pack test leaves out of a biome's modded share: they only spawn underground, after the Wither, or under a condition of their own.

skip_dependencies._comment: Projects a mod's Modrinth page lists as required that the pack leaves out, each with why (its jar works without them).
skip_dependencies.plasmo-voice: Voiceless Survival lists both voice chat mods as required, but works with either; the pack's voice chat is Simple Voice Chat (FreshOrangeSlices, 2026-10-30), and a second voice mod would put its own keys and server port next to it.

client_presets._resource_packs: Bottom to top, above vanilla's Default (and Forge's mod resources). Bloom switches them on before the game first reads options.txt, once per change of this list (client/mixin/OptionsMixin).
client_presets._shader: Shaders on with Complementary Unbound at first launch (and once per change of this line); K turns shaders off, O picks another pack (Solas and the much lighter MakeUp Ultra Fast ship too).

keys._keys_chunk6: FreshOrangeSlices, 2026-10-30: one job per key where it matters. Z is the dodge roll alone, V Bloom's weapon skill alone, C Iron's cast, R (hold) Iron's spell wheel; armor abilities share a key per slot (a player wears one helmet, one chestplate, one pair of boots); Soulslike's weapon actions share N (each only acts with its own weapon). Migamigos' six keys do nothing (its code never reads them). Dragon-riding, taming and JEI keys only act in their own context, so they keep theirs.
keys._keys_voice: Simple Voice Chat (FreshOrangeSlices, 2026-10-30): push-to-talk on Caps Lock (it has no key of its own, and its setup wizard is skipped), its menu on Ctrl+V and groups on Ctrl+G (V is Bloom's weapon skill, G Curios), mute on Shift+M (M is Xaero's world map), turning voice off on Shift+N (N is Soulslike's), its hide-icons key off (H is the helmet abilities').

client_presets._keys: Key bindings, each set once per change of it (by name, as options.txt has them; a player's own change afterwards stays): Oculus's 'reload shaders' is unbound (it was R, and a stray press freezes the game for seconds while the shader rebuilds), and Keybind Atlas opens on Ctrl+K (it started on K, Oculus's shader toggle; Alt+K is its own 'cycle keybind sets'). Combat Roll is the one dodge, on Z (FreshOrangeSlices); Bosses'Rise's and Monster Expansion's rolls are switched off (config_files) and their keys unbound, so the Controls list has no live second dodge.

settings._comment: Settings in other mods' client config files, each set once per change of it, the rest of the file left as the player has it (Bloom's PackDefaults: a .json key is a / path, IPN keeping each option as {"value": ...}; a .toml key has its [Section] in front). A file that isn't there yet is started with these lines and the mod fills in the rest. FreshOrangeSlices' playtest: a simple craft screen (no Crafting Tweaks buttons, which keep their keys; no IPN auto-crafting checkbox; no IPN profiles), and tools that break like in normal Minecraft (IPN's auto-refill off, with all its warnings). Bosses'Rise's roll indicator by the hotbar is hidden (its roll is off; Combat Roll has its own).

sidebar_buttons.json._comment: FTB Library's buttons at the inventory's top-left: the quest book and FTB Teams stay; its four op-only cheat buttons (game mode, rain, day, night) are off, since they overlapped the buttons below them (FreshOrangeSlices' screenshot, 2026-10-30). Ops still have the commands.

voicechat/voicechat-client.properties._comment: Simple Voice Chat ready on first join: its setup wizard counted as done (config_version must be there too, or it migrates the file and sets the wizard back), push-to-talk (its default) on the pack's Caps Lock key.

patches._comment: The same, for a file a mod starts from the pack's defaultconfigs/ copy on a first start (so a new install has these already and an older one gets them once): Xaero's Minimap locked north and round.

copies._comment: Whole files copied over a mod's own once per change of their content. Xaero's Minimap's radar colors (FreshOrangeSlices: hostile red, passive green, neutral yellow, your own pets sky blue, players as their heads, no dropped items or projectiles, bigger dots): its default categories file, which every minimap profile without radar categories of its own reads. Neutral is a category of its own (mobs that only fight back), ahead of Hostile so endermen and piglins land there; tamed mobs anywhere are sky blue. Colors are Minecraft's chat colors by number (10 green, 11 aqua, 12 red, 14 yellow, 15 white). A "file:" value is a file under pack/files.

files._comment: Client config files, as given (the mod fills in every setting left out). A file under defaultconfigs/ is a mod's default, copied in only where the player has no config of their own yet (so an update never resets their settings). FreshOrangeSlices wants Minecraft's own title screen: Aquamirae swaps in its frozen-sea panorama and logo. Inventory Profiles Next's sort buttons sat on top of the Spell Binding Table's spell list (FreshOrangeSlices' playtest): an IPN hint switches IPN off on that screen (the table has nothing to sort).
files.defaultconfigs/xaero/minimap/profiles/de:
# Warionex: the minimap keeps north at the top instead of turning with you, and is round (FreshOrangeSlices). Xaero's Minimap copies this into config/xaero/minimap/profiles/ on a first start and fills in every other setting; after that it's the player's own (Minimap Settings, Lock Minimap North).
profile_name = Default
minimap_north_locked = true
minimap_shape = 1
